primitives.name: Government Schools Football Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: 65 FOOTBALL THE ARMY AND NAVY For many years the annual games between the elevens representing the United States government's military and naval schools have created great interest in football circles.
primitives.assumptions: (1) The model assumes that both West Point and Annapolis maintain consistent team rosters over time. (2) It assumes that the quality of players is directly proportional to the academic rigor of the institutions. (3) The model assumes that the annual game follows a fixed structure without rule changes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The model breaks down when external factors (e.g., wars, pandemics) disrupt normal attendance and roster stability.

layer2.mapping: Maps the sovereign primitive to a conformal prediction set for game outcomes, where the historical performance of smaller, elite institutions serves as a prior distribution for predicting competitive parity against larger universities.
layer2.telemetry: Observed win rates of West Point and Annapolis against major university schedules serve as empirical validation metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is to mathematically capture the paradox of producing world-class athletes from a constrained, highly selective enrollment base. The sovereign primitive "Government Schools Football Model" establishes a foundational observation: despite small squad sizes, these institutions achieve exceptional competitive parity. This is formalized through a constrained optimization lens, treating the total player pool as a fixed budget. The primitive "West Point vs. Princeton System" introduces a dualistic constraint: West Point operates under a resource-limited, physical paradigm, while Annapolis functions within an information-theoretic, passing-focused regime. Their coexistence creates a robust ecosystem where neither style dominates absolutely. Finally, the primitive "Small School Elite Pool" provides the mechanism for sustained excellence, acting as a natural regularizer that prevents overfitting to any single strategy. Together, these primitives form a unified triad: the optimization problem (Government Schools Model) is solved by balancing diverse tactical approaches (West Point/Princeton Dichotomy), all powered by a steady influx of high-quality, filtered talent (Small School Elite Pool). Failure occurs when the filtering mechanism weakens, leading to a degradation of the entire system. This unification aligns with modern sports analytics' shift toward integrated behavioral-skill models.

reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity condition: The three primitives must operate on distinct layers—optimization (Government Schools Model), tactics (West Point/Princeton Dichotomy), and talent (Small School Elite Pool)—to avoid redundant information.
